title: Nadine Gordimer's birth chart
metaDescription: Nadine Gordimer's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 27.1° Scorpio. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a conjunction: Mercury and Jupiter within 0.5°, thinking wired to expansion. A conjunction is the least negotiable aspect in the scheme — no distance to argue across, so the pair arrives as a single instinct.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 27.1° Scorpio — the third decan, 20°–30°, which the tradition sub-rules by the Moon. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Scorpio and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Closer in, Venus stands at 15.2° Sagittarius; Mars stands at 21.2° Libra. The tradition reads taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate from Venus, drive that argues its way forward from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Closest first: Mercury to Jupiter, a conjunction with 0.5° of slack. When two functions occupy one degree, the tradition reads a fusion: neither can act without committing the other. Behind it, Mars sextile Neptune at 0.8°, and Uranus trine Pluto at 1.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The day-stable angles form no closed figure. Nothing funnels; each aspect is its own negotiation, which the tradition reads as a chart of separate treaties rather than one campaign.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The classical table has two entries for this chart. Mars in Libra at 21.2° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Libra at 27.1° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives water 4, fire 3, air 2, and cardinal 4, fixed 3, mutable 2 across the modes. A water emphasis keeps long books: little is forgotten, and nothing is felt only once. Mercury crossed from Scorpio into Sagittarius during that day, so its sign is left open. No settled placement falls in earth — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Uranus and Pluto were retrograde — the backward drift a body appears to make as the Earth overtakes it, read in the scheme as a function that reviews before it releases.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Aries for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 11.9° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 23.1°.
